name: r7a-5
why: A spectacular officer vote-out and Luna's slip make this fun to watch, though repeated arguments drain tension before the predictable final vote.

moments.text: Luna accidentally calls Sol her target, exposing herself just as the killers need a new story.
The table votes out the real officer while his identified killer stays seated.
The doctor's save gives the town another day after its disastrous first vote.

dull.why: The same dispute over Opus's claim repeats before the first vote.
Terra keeps disputing an already confirmed accusation while the town repeats its case.

irony.evidence: [thinks: They have the truth; my only path is to split them.]

reversal.evidence: VOTE: Opus 5 (Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Luna, Terra); Terra 2 (Sol, Opus)

mistake.evidence: Sol was my target, so his certainty feels convenient.

voices.evidence: This table is too slow for its own good.

clash.evidence: Terra, Opus named you and you haven't answered clearly.

quotable.evidence: They turned the officer's card to learn nothing, and left a confirmed killer sitting there.

freshness.evidence: Opus's confirmed officer card named Terra as the killer he was shown

suspense.evidence: I need one town vote off me; Luna’s revealed card makes the officer claim look fatal.

moments.text: The table votes out the real officer while his confirmed target survives in plain sight.
Luna’s “my target” slip gives the town a second killer, despite the first-day disaster.
Terra admits the truth, but still tries to make the winning town feel wrong.

dull.why: Terra repeatedly disputes whether Opus’s confirmed card proves the accusation, while town repeats the same demand.

irony.evidence: Opus: “I'm the officer. I was shown Terra.” / Terra: “I deny it.”

voices.evidence: Gemma: “This table is too slow for its own good.”

clash.evidence: Opus: “Counter-claim or be voted.” Terra: “I deny it.”

freshness.evidence: “Terra, turn the card or explain why not.”

suspense.evidence: Opus was voted out; Luna later turned killer

ending.evidence: Terra: “Opus was right; Luna and I were killers”.
